To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the largest enhancements for the gg → hSM → γγ and gg → hSMZZ rates in the two-Higgs-doublets model are ~1.3 and ~0.8, respectively, while the corresponding values for gg → h → gg → γγ and for gg → hSMgg → ZZ are ~1.6 and ~0.9, respectively.

(1) the gg → h (125 GeV) → γγ rate can be enhanced by up to ~ 1.4 relative to that for gg → hSM (125 GeV), and (2) the gg → H (125 GeV → γγ rate cannot be enhanced by more than a factor of ~ 1.2 relative to that for hSM.
the Type II model is excluded for mH± > ~ 150 GeV and the Type I model is disfavored for mH± < ~ 90 GeV and tan β = 20.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: how large can the enhancement of the γγ rate for the 125 GeV boson be while remaining consistent with all experimental constraints and with the requirement of perturbativity and vacuum stability?
the question: can one have a 125 Gev Higgs with an enhancement of the γγ mode relative to the SM rate without a large enhancement of other Higgs modes?
the possibility of observing a 125 Gev Higgs boson with a rate for the γγ or ZZ final states that is substantially enhanced relative to the rate for the SM H → γγ or H → ZZ mode.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current data are not inconsistent with a 125 Gev Higgs in a Type I two-Higgs-double model, but that the current LHC data disfavor a large enhancement in the gg → hSMγγ rate in Type II models.
the 125 GeV signal in γγ is consistent with the Standard Model and that a large enhancement in the γγ channel would be accompanied by an enhanced ZZ rate.
the current data disfavor a two-Higgs-Doublet model Higgs with mass near 124 GeV that has a gg → H → gg signal rate enhanced by more than a factor of 2 relative to that of the SM Higgs boson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current data are already in a position to rule out a large class of models with two Higgs doublets, and that the prospects for discovering a light Higgs boson at the Tevatron are much improved relative to the SM Higgs boson.
the current data are consistent with a 125 GeVin Higgs boson with the same properties as the SM Higgs boson, with the exception of the gg → γγ mode, which may be enhanced by a factor of 2.
the two-Higgs-doublets can enhance the gg → Higgs → γγ signal, but only at the expense of having an even larger gg → Higgs boson → ZZ signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC will be able to probe the two-Higgs-double model Higgs sector in a very direct manner, with little need for theoretical assumptions.
, in contrast with the case of the SM-like Higgs boson with mass near 120 GeV, the 125 GeV two-Higgs-double models are not expected to have enhanced rates in the gg → h, H → γγ channel.

, while the LHC can probe a significant portion of the parameter space for a light 125 GeV SM-like Higgs, a heavy Higgs with mass near 600 GeV is not likely to be found with a large rate enhancement in the γγ or ZZ final states.
